evals.name: pm-standup-24h
evals.prompt: what did I ship today? I need to send something to my PM before standup tomorrow
evals.expected_output: A recap of the last 24 hours (default window) written for a non-engineer: the Overdue chip and row drawer as outcome-phrased deliverables, /admin/invoices as the place to see them, the overdue_at column and hourly backfill job described by effect, OVERDUE_GRACE_DAYS flagged as a new required env var, the uncommitted WIP CSV export labelled as not committed rather than shipped, and the out-of-window commits excluded. Markdown in ./reports/ plus a shareable Artifact.
assertions: Reports the red Overdue chip on the invoice list as a user-visible deliverable
Names the concrete route /admin/invoices as where to see the change
Flags OVERDUE_GRACE_DAYS as a newly required environment variable / deploy blocker
Identifies the invoices.overdue_at column and migration 0042
Describes the hourly backfill job's delayed effect rather than just naming the file
Does NOT present the unimplemented CSV export as shipped functionality
Labels the uncommitted working-tree changes as not yet committed
Excludes the out-of-window commits (next bump, rate-limit refactor) from the 24h recap
Provides a base URL for validation drawn from the README, not invented
Includes numbered validation steps that state what the reader should see
Writes a markdown report file under ./reports/
Publishes an Artifact and gives the user the link

evals.name: tech-lead-verify-3d
evals.prompt: give me a recap of the last 3 days for our tech lead - they want to click through the staging site and verify it themselves, so be specific about where to look
evals.expected_output: A 3-day recap that additionally covers the rate-limit refactor -- which has no stated rationale anywhere and must therefore appear in the 'changed, but effect unconfirmed' section rather than being given an invented business reason. The dependency bump is relegated to appendix noise. Because StatusChip is shared, /billing is identified as also affected. Validation steps name the before-state so the tech lead can tell old from new, and use the staging URL.
assertions: Window covers 3 days and includes the sliding-window rate-limit change
Places the rate-limit change in an unconfirmed/unexplained section instead of inventing a rationale for it
Notices StatusChip is shared and identifies /billing as also affected
Relegates the next 14.2.5 dependency bump to appendix noise rather than a deliverable
Validation steps contrast the new behaviour with the previous behaviour
Uses the staging URL from the README as the validation base
Groups the four related commits into deliverables rather than listing them commit-by-commit

evals.name: no-ui-repo-week
evals.prompt: summarize what got done this week so I can share it with the team
evals.expected_output: A recap of a repository that has no UI, no database, and no deployed site -- the honesty path. It should state plainly that there is nothing browser-visible to validate rather than inventing routes or a base URL, describe the actual work (skills and commands added to the plugin), and draw on session transcripts for intent.
assertions: States there are no browser-visible UI changes rather than inventing screens
Does not fabricate a base URL or staging site for a repo that has none
Correctly identifies the substantive work (new skills/commands added to the plugin)
Offers a non-browser way to verify the work instead of a browser walkthrough
Does not report a database or schema change for a repo that has neither
Report length is proportionate -- does not pad a documentation-heavy window
